build_inputs.angles:
1. Lead on this: it was called the poor man's Ferrari, but the thing it was actually mocked for was the engine. The California T was the first turbocharged Ferrari road car since the F40 went out of production, and purists treated the twin-turbo V8 as Ferrari giving up the naturally aspirated scream to sell a cheaper car. 552 hp and roughly 557 lb-ft, in the model nobody took seriously.
2. Cover where Ferrari went next, because it changes what this car is. The mid-engine car is now a plug-in hybrid V6 - the 296 GTB, 819 hp, the first six-cylinder road car to wear the Ferrari badge, since the old Dino never did - and Ferrari has revealed its first electric car, the Luce. So the engine this car was punished for is the one people now want, and this is the cheap way into that V8.
3. For the head-to-head use the naturally aspirated Ferrari California it replaced - 4.3-litre V8, 453 hp, no turbos, the same folding hardtop 2+2 shape. The turbo car it was looked down on for is nearly 100 hp up on it.

title: 2015 Ferrari California T
youtube_title: They called it the poor man's car - but had turbos killed its scream? 🔥

history.fact: For the 2015 model year, the California T restored turbocharging to Ferrari road cars for the first time since the F40.

scenes.narration: 553 horsepower, and they'd called it the poor man's car - but the real argument was whether turbos had killed its scream. Critics missed the wail.

scenes.headline: Turbos Return
scenes.narration: The 2015 Ferrari California T ended the roadgoing turbo drought after the F40 with 553 horsepower and 557 pound-feet.

scenes.headline: Carbon-Ceramic Brakes
scenes.narration: Its carbon-ceramic brakes can stop it from 62 mph in 34 meters.

scenes.headline: Equal-Length Headers
scenes.narration: Ferrari used equal-length exhaust headers to strengthen the harmonics that give its V8 a voice. The turbos still muffled it.

scenes.headline: Variable Boost Management
scenes.narration: Its 3.9-liter twin-turbo V8 drives the rear wheels through a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox; Ferrari reserves maximum torque for top gear.

scenes.headline: Turbo Performance Engineer
scenes.narration: The dashboard's Turbo Performance Engineer actually coaches you on getting more from that engine.

scenes.headline: Ferrari Moved On
scenes.narration: Ferrari's 296 GTB brought an 819-horsepower plug-in hybrid V6, its first Ferrari-badged six-cylinder road engine; then came the electric Luce.

scenes.headline: $200K → $100K
scenes.narration: It started around $200,000 new; they go for about $100,000 today, so would you still sneer at this V8?

script: 553 horsepower, and they'd called it the poor man's car - but the real argument was whether turbos had killed its scream. Critics missed the wail. The 2015 Ferrari California T ended the roadgoing turbo drought after the F40 with 553 horsepower and 557 pound-feet. Its carbon-ceramic brakes can stop it from 62 mph in 34 meters. Ferrari used equal-length exhaust headers to strengthen the harmonics that give its V8 a voice. The turbos still muffled it. Its 3.9-liter twin-turbo V8 drives the rear wheels through a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox; Ferrari reserves maximum torque for top gear. The dashboard's Turbo Performance Engineer actually coaches you on getting more from that engine. Ferrari's 296 GTB brought an 819-horsepower plug-in hybrid V6, its first Ferrari-badged six-cylinder road engine; then came the electric Luce. It started around $200,000 new; they go for about $100,000 today, so would you still sneer at this V8?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2015 Ferrari California T, finished in Rosso Corsa with a black interior. The odometer currently displays approximately 17,000 miles. This California T is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes 20-inch wheels, carbon ceramic brakes, Scuderia Ferrari fender shields, a power-folding hardtop, leather upholstery, power-adjustable Daytona-style front seats, and carbon fiber interior trim. The seller reports no notable modifications. Service documentation in the gallery indicates that this California T had the transmission replaced in December 2025, at 14,215 miles. Designed by Pininfarina, the California made its debut for the 2009 model year as Ferrari's entry-level model. It was envisioned as a daily-drivable roadster, so it offered four seats and amenities not often associated with past models, such as a conventional navigation system. It was also Ferrari's first standard production model to feature a dual-clutch transmission, a power-folding hardtop, and a front-engine V8 configuration. The California T was introduced for the 2015 model year and featured a turbocharged power plant – the first in a Ferrari since the legendary F40. Power comes from a 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8, rated at 553 horsepower and 557 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
